originalText:
The main “problem with Fable” right now (as of June 13, 2026) is that Anthropic was forced to completely disable its brand-new Claude Fable 5 model (and the related Mythos 5) for all users after a sudden US government export control directive.0
What Happened (Timeline)
• June 9, 2026: Anthropic launches Claude Fable 5 (a “Mythos-class” model made safe for general use) and Claude Mythos 5 (more powerful, initially for trusted partners/gov use). Fable 5 was positioned as their strongest publicly available model yet — excelling at long-horizon reasoning, coding, finance, and agentic tasks.14

• June 12 evening (Friday 5:21pm ET): US Commerce Department (under Secretary Howard Lutnick) issues a directive citing national security. It orders Anthropic to block access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for all foreign nationals (inside or outside the US, including Anthropic’s own foreign employees).

• Anthropic says complying requires shutting it down for everyone (they can’t reliably check user nationalities in real time). They disabled the models abruptly and publicly complained that the gov provided no detailed rationale beyond a “narrow potential jailbreak” risk.

This comes on top of Anthropic’s existing tensions with the Pentagon (the earlier blacklist/supply-chain-risk label from the guardrails dispute).

Additional Backlash (“Problems” Before the Shutdown)?

Well even before the gov forced it offline, Fable 5 drew heavy criticism:

• Secret/hidden safeguards → It would silently degrade performance on prompts related to frontier AI development, pretraining, or certain research (called “secret sabotage” by some researchers). Anthropic later walked some of this back and made safeguards more visible after the outcry.

• Overly strict refusals and capability limits in sensitive areas (cyber, biology, etc.).

• High pricing and mixed user reception on whether the “safety” trade-offs were worth it.

Bottom line: Fable 5 became the flashpoint for ongoing Anthropic vs. US gov friction... safety philosophy clashing with national security/export controls. The model is currently offline, and it’s unclear when (or if) it returns. This escalated very quickly after launch.

originalText:
[Claude Fable system prompt leaks - on SEO/GEO]

"Get on Reddit for AI visibility" is everywhere right now. The leaked Claude Fable 5 prompt says the opposite.

Here's what its search instructions actually prioritize:

1️⃣ It skips forums by default
↳ "Skip low-quality sources like forums unless specifically relevant."
↳ Reddit is not a free pass here.

2️⃣ It prefers primary sources
↳ Company blogs, peer-reviewed papers, government and SEC filings.
↳ Your own domain ranks above the forum talking about you.

3️⃣ This is the mirror image of Google
↳ Google has pushed Reddit to the top since its helpful content updates.
↳ Same brand, opposite source preference, two different engines.

The lesson isn't "Reddit is dead."

It's that GEO is not one playbook. The only bet that pays off everywhere is being a primary source on a domain you own.

Every successful subscription business is built on the fact that people will use a small % of theoretical max

Otherwise they would be in the usage business instead

When I worked in tech, the rule of thumb was that only around 5-10% of users would be power users, while anywhere up to 50% of users would basically never use the product

The question is whether in the long term the revenue will shift more and more to a usage model, like they are sort of testing with Fable 5 later this month

title: Claude Fable 5 availability update
author: Krish Subramanian
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5 launch is less interesting as a benchmark story and more interesting as a product governance story.

The headline is simple. Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 on June 9 and says it is the most capable model it has made generally available. It also launched Claude Mythos 5 for a smaller group of cyberdefenders and infrastructure providers.

The part worth watching is the release design.

Anthropic says Fable 5 will route some queries to Claude Opus 4.8 when safeguards trigger. It also says those safeguards trigger in less than 5 percent of sessions on average. Pricing is $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, with subscription access changing after an initial included window.

That tells us where frontier model deployment is going.

It is no longer just “ship the smartest model.” It is model routing, access tiers, capacity windows, policy controls, and trust segmentation.

Enterprise buyers should pay attention to this pattern. The operational question is not whether the model is impressive. It probably is.

The Day 2 question is more practical:

Can your workflow tolerate safety routing, changing access windows, cost spikes, and capability differences by user class?

For healthcare, financial services, government, and critical infrastructure, this matters a lot. If a model silently falls back or refuses part of a workflow, you need observability, auditability, and a designed escalation path.

Otherwise your “AI transformation” becomes a very expensive guessing game. Always fun in a production environment.

#EnterpriseAI #AISafety #AIInfrastructure #AIGovernance #HealthcareAI #CIO #AITransformation

title: Claude Fable 5 availability update
author: Ole Herland (Odett.ai)
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
The cracks are starting to show. Today is a bleak day to live in EU 😐

I woke up exited to continue my work with the latest and strongest model from Anthropic, Fable 5. For some reason it wasn't available. Then I saw this statement from the US gov.

"Access is suspended for any foreign national, wether inside or outside the United States."

This could be the beginning of an era where access to the latest and best models gets restricted more and more. Where only certain countries, companies or people have access.

If we are really unlucky, then this is going to increase the imbalance that we are already facing today. Be it power or money.

If we are lucky, open source alternatives starts getting stronger and stronger.

This brings me to why this is a bleak day to live in the EU.

The US is starting to limit the access to models built by their companies.
The Chinese might start doing the same soon.
This leaves us in the middle. With no access.

As you probably know. The EU is not famous for being forward leaning in terms of technology. Sure, we have some nice tech here and there. But we lagg so far behind, especially when it comes to AI.

I hope we take this as a warning. As a sign that we need to do much more to make AI generally available for all. To make it a common good 🙌🏻

Note: For now it seams like the model is restricted for everyone (globally). Not sure if this is because they just don't have the tools yet to segment access. But the message is still the same.

title: 30-day data retention mandatory made with Fable 5
author: Burak Sormagec
verification: Fetched from X via twitter-cli from global-search; original author and post URL preserved.
note: Original post did not expose a complete repeatable prompt. Treat this as a real showcase post, not a verified tutorial.
originalText:
Microsoft restricted Claude Fable 5 for employees before most engineers even saw the changelog.

That tells you everything.

Anthropic just made 30-day data retention mandatory for all Mythos-class models — Fable, Mythos, and whatever comes next. Even if you paid for Zero Data Retention. Even on AWS Bedrock and Azure Foundry. Even in Claude Code where your entire codebase gets sent as context.

The official reason is safety. These models can do real cybersecurity work, so Anthropic wants to catch jailbreaks, distillation attempts, and state-sponsored abuse. Reasonable on paper.

But the ground truth is messier:

→ Microsoft — Anthropic's own partner — banned it internally for "legal review" the same day it launched

→ Cybersecurity researchers report Fable auto-downgrades to Opus when you say words like... "cybersecurity" (yes, really)

→ ZDR contracts just became "ZDR unless we need 30 days, which is always"

This isn't safety vs. capability. It's surveillance packaged as trust.

And it's a trend, not a one-off. Every frontier lab is converging on the same model: the "free/cheap" tier gets privacy theater, while the actually-capable models come with mandatory data retention and opaque human review.

Enterprises are waking up to the bait-and-switch. Anthropic spent years selling itself as the "privacy-friendly" AI company. Now their own partners won't touch their flagship model internally.

If you're building an AI strategy for a company that actually cares about IP, NDAs, or regulatory compliance, here's the only assumption that holds: treat every prompt to a cloud frontier model as potentially retained, readable, and subpoena-able.

ZDR was a contract clause, not a technical guarantee.

The hedge isn't switching providers. It's local inference, self-hosted pipelines, and contractual carve-outs that don't rely on a vendor's goodwill.

Because goodwill evaporates the moment "safety" enters the room.

https://t.co/y7VTQATNuX

#AI #CyberSecurity
